Done. The council page is rebuilt for desktop and chat-only layouts, with the 40×20 floor, the owner's director's office and the new behaviour. Typecheck, the two test files (57 tests) and the build all pass.

**Changed paths** (all inside `owns_paths`; nothing else touched):
- `src/rooms/council/ui/office-layout.ts`: 40×20 grid, walls and doorways, every prop footprint and interaction point from reference.md, 10 meeting chairs, 8 desks, the owner's home/window/bar spots, A* on the new grid, and the simulation with owner and report rules.
- `src/rooms/council/ui/office-scene.ts`: slab, zones, walls, windows and doors, furniture per room, exterior lot, lights.
- `src/rooms/council/ui/office-behaviour.ts`: actors (owner always present; speaks only under his own message), label collisions at 30 %, camera fit from reference.md §4, pose and walk helpers.
- `src/rooms/council/ui/council-office.tsx`: three.js floor with the reference camera, owner walk to the table with the 15 s hold and replay snapping, report yield, disposal on unmount.
- `src/rooms/council/ui/council-page.tsx`: desktop (≥1024) is the office with a floating top bar, a collapsed-by-default drawer (380/340 px, state in localStorage) and a peek card. Below 1024 it is the chat page. The office loads via `React.lazy` only on desktop.
- `tests/council-office.test.ts`, `tests/council-page.test.tsx`: rewritten for the new grid and rules, and each view picked by mocking the block width.

**Rules I set aside:** none. The project rules about owns_paths were followed.

**Decisions and deviations**
- The drawer, when open, takes the right side, so the office canvas covers the block minus the drawer rather than the whole block. I did this instead of changing `CouncilOffice` props, which the contract forbids. The camera refits to that area.
- The seat disclosure shows only the seat count, and the closed-council line reuses the state label. `packages/i18n` is outside owns_paths and has no "Participants" or "closed" key, so I added no strings.
- The decision toggle is a chevron for the same reason.

**Gaps**
- **Not verified visually.** Tests run in jsdom with the WebGL fallback, so the three.js scene, camera and tag layout were only typechecked and built, never rendered. Look against reference.jpg in a browser before accepting.
- **three.js is inlined in `dist/app.js`** (~4.3 MB, `WebGLRenderer` present). The `import("three")` call only runs on desktop, but the bytes are parsed on every page load. Splitting needs a bundler change outside owns_paths.
- **Characters avoid each other only by yielding:** a walker waits up to 2.5 s when a standing character blocks its next step. There is no true path avoidance between people.
- **Live reply hold is not implemented.** The owner's replay hold covers replies within two messages, but live only applies the 15 s hold after he speaks.
- **Not done:** the drawer doesn't auto-open when a decision arrives.

Turn the council office into a full-width band showing a whole isometric office floor whose props carry geodata (footprints and interaction points), with properly drawn pixel characters that live a purposeful office life: long stays at their own desk, coffee, sofa, window, chats, all without walking through objects, and gather in the meeting room when the council is in session.
- 2026-10-09T10:37 council-office-rework: Council office rework: non-overlapping labels, wandering after replay pause, art matching the reference. Fix the three live QA failures of the council office: name labels overlap up to 85%, characters stay frozen after a replay is paused, and the room art renders tan/olive and tiny instead of the bright peach/yellow diorama with visible projector screen, glass door, bins and readable characters.
- 2026-10-09T09:52 council-office-art: Council office art pass: bright isometric cutaway diorama with outlines and detailed props (owner reference). Restyle the council office to match the owner's reference: a bright isometric cutaway room on a light background with a thick floor slab, two light walls with baseboard stripe, dark pixel outlines, a long meeting table with laptops and office chairs, projector screen, whiteboard, glass door, cabinet, bins, boxes and clutter, and properly coloured characters, with the whole room framed in view.
- 2026-10-09T09:46 council-office-qa-fixes: Council page: bounded wide header, bubbles/labels inside office, distinct seat colors, moderator notice. Fix the live browser QA defects of the council page: at 1280 px the unbounded header hides office, log and composer; speech bubbles clip at the office top and show raw markdown; name labels overlap and clip; two seats share a color; moderator messages have no presence; the reset button squeezes the project select at 375 px.
- 2026-10-09T09:37 council-office-characters: Council office: characters walk, sit, talk and gesture like people (no teleporting). Make the council office characters believable: they walk at a steady speed along paths around furniture instead of teleporting, sit in visible chairs at the table, stand up and talk with gesturing arms and typewriter speech bubbles, face and point at the seat they argue with, react while listening, and in free time stroll to office spots and do small actions (coffee, window, typing at a desk), with replay steps driving the same walked motion.
- 2026-10-09T08:59 council-office-live: Council page: always-on pixel-art three.js office with pixel-styled history and replay. Make the Council page an always-on isometric pixel-art office on three.js where seats (plus chair and owner) are blocky characters who speak at the meeting table with bubbles, face the seat they answer, wait seated, and wander when idle; next to it the conversation history is a pixel-art styled log linked to the office, with a replay that plays a past council message by message.
